Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0086", "row_sha256": "cf0ece1493fa6a3372b9a55a07c2f7bead32fc5608d3600d4d3e1df2cb16c6ce", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn these notes into a clear prompt for a detailed product brief about a preference in a browser extension. the fictional extension is called Fieldnote and coordinators use it to review vendor entries in a side panel while they work. this is about one preference, not a redesign of the extension or a general review workflow. the preference is for how the list of entries looks, and the basic choice is compact or comfortable density. i'm not asking for code or finished interface copy here, i need a prompt that asks for a brief someone could use to plan the change.

the settings page is already in the extension, and the new control belongs under Settings, then Appearance. call it “Review layout.” comfortable is selected by default for both existing and new users. compact makes each entry card shorter by reducing the vertical space around its contents; it should still show the vendor name, current status, and date in the card. comfortable keeps the current spacing and is easier to scan when someone wants more room between entries. don't turn compact into a different information hierarchy, and don't hide one of those three items to make the card fit. the prompt should ask for a short explanation of both choices in the brief, not polished final UI strings.

this must stay a view preference. do not modify records. a person changing the setting may change card density and may expand or collapse a record preview, but the choice must not edit vendor names, status, dates, or any other stored vendor information. opening a record to view its details is also still allowed, and the brief can make that distinction clear. the existing action that opens the vendor’s page on the company website is unrelated and should not be presented as something this preference changes. don't imply that selecting compact updates, cleans up, or saves changes to a vendor entry. the request is not to add an editing function.

save the selected density in the browser profile on that device so it remains selected when Fieldnote is closed and reopened. don't describe it as an account setting or say it follows a person to another device; that behavior isn't part of these notes. if someone selects “Restore defaults” in the existing appearance settings, return Review layout to comfortable. that reset should apply to this preference along with the other appearance defaults, not erase vendor entries or change their details. don't invent a separate reset control just for Review layout. if the brief needs to explain the setting's persistence or reset behavior, use these details as the full scope.

for the interaction, the user opens Settings, selects Appearance, and chooses either comfortable or compact from a two-option control. the display updates in the side panel, without requiring a page reload. show how the brief should describe the immediate visual change without claiming that data has been saved or altered. changing the choice back and forth should be reversible. don't add a confirmation dialog; there is no confirmation step in the current flow. a person can still expand or collapse a preview while either density is selected. those previews are temporary viewing behavior, not another saved preference, and don't change the underlying entry.

include accessibility in a practical way but keep it tied to this control: the option names should be understandable when read by assistive technology, the selected choice should be conveyed without relying on color alone, and the control should be usable with a keyboard. don't prescribe a particular component library or claim that Fieldnote already meets a specific accessibility standard. The browser panel also has a narrow width, so mention that the required vendor name, status, and date remain readable at the available panel width in both choices. Don't propose removing the date or replacing it with an icon just to save space.

there was a comment from a coordinator during an informal review: “I usually leave more breathing room, but compact helps when I’m checking a long list.” treat that as a user observation, not evidence that everyone wants compact, and don't turn it into a product metric or a promise about speed. the brief can use it to explain why both densities exist. keep the tone practical and neutral; we don't need marketing language, a success story, or claims about improved productivity. distinguish the single-person choice from any default that applies to someone who has not changed it.

please structure the prompt so the requested brief covers: 1. the purpose and location of Review layout; 2. the two choices, the default, and what changes visually; 3. the permitted actions and the boundary that records are not changed; 4. persistence and Restore defaults; and 5. interaction and accessibility details. ask for a concise but useful brief, with those details easy to find. It should call out what is explicitly in scope and avoid suggesting account sync, analytics, new controls, vendor editing, or a broader redesign. Those are not decisions to explore in this brief. Don't make the brief itself into implementation code or final UI copy.

end the requested brief with a distinct note about the existing vendor-page link: it remains as it is and is outside this preference. keep that separate from the description of the density control so no one reads the link as part of the new setting. the final prompt should ask for the brief only, not answer the product question or add recommendations beyond these notes.", "output": "Write a concise, useful product brief for the **Review layout** preference in the fictional Fieldnote browser extension. Coordinators use Fieldnote to review vendor entries in a side panel. Cover this preference only; do not propose a redesign of the extension or its general review workflow. The brief is for planning the change, not for producing code or finished interface copy.

### 1. Purpose and location
Place the control under **Settings > Appearance**. It changes the visual density of the entry list in the side panel. Briefly explain the purpose of offering both choices, using the coordinator’s observation as context: “I usually leave more breathing room, but compact helps when I’m checking a long list.” Treat this as one person’s observation, not evidence of a universal preference, a product metric, or a promise about speed. Keep the tone practical and neutral rather than promotional.

### 2. Choices and visual behavior
The control is called **Review layout** and offers two choices: **comfortable** and **compact**. Comfortable is the default for both existing and new users. It keeps the current spacing and provides more room between entries. Compact reduces the vertical space around the contents of each entry card, making the cards shorter. In both choices, the card must continue to show the vendor name, current status, and date. Do not change the information hierarchy or hide any of those items to make a card fit. Mention that all three remain readable in the panel’s narrow width. Request a short explanation of each choice, not polished final UI strings.

### 3. Scope and record behavior
This is a view preference. **do not modify records**. A person may change card density or expand and collapse a record preview, but neither action edits vendor names, statuses, dates, or other stored vendor information. Opening a record to view its details remains allowed. Make clear that preview expansion and collapse are temporary viewing behavior, not a separately saved preference. Do not imply that selecting compact updates, cleans up, or saves changes to a vendor entry, and do not add an editing function.

### 4. Persistence and reset
Save the selected density in the browser profile on that device so it remains selected when Fieldnote is closed and reopened. Do not describe it as an account setting or say that it follows a person to another device. The existing **Restore defaults** action in Appearance returns Review layout to comfortable along with the other appearance defaults. It does not erase vendor entries or change their details. Do not introduce a separate reset control for Review layout.

### 5. Interaction and accessibility
Describe the flow: a user opens Settings, selects Appearance, and chooses comfortable or compact from a two-option control. The side-panel display updates without a page reload, and the choice can be changed back and forth without a confirmation dialog. Do not claim that changing density saves or alters vendor data. Cover the control’s practical accessibility needs: option names are understandable when read by assistive technology, the selected choice is conveyed without relying on color alone, and the control works with a keyboard. Do not prescribe a component library or claim compliance with a particular accessibility standard.

Keep the requested brief focused on the details above. Do not add account sync, analytics, new controls, vendor editing, or a broader redesign. Do not turn the brief into implementation code or final interface copy.

End with a distinct note that the existing action opening a vendor’s page on the company website remains as it is and is outside this preference. Keep that note separate from the density control so the link is not mistaken for part of the new setting."}]
